mainTopic: Which fruits are fit for ביכורים, עולא's ruling that inferior fruit brought as ביכורים does not become holy, and the start of רבי אחא בר אבא's objection to רבה from a ברייתא about the שתי הלחם coming first
overview: The amud opens with the rule that ביכורים are not brought from mountain dates or from valley fruit. עולא adds that if someone brought the inferior fruit anyway, it does not become holy. רבי אחא בר אבא challenges this from a long ברייתא. That ברייתא says the שתי הלחם must come before every new crop, even crops grown on a roof, in a ruin, in a flowerpot or on a ship. רבה answers that this part of the ברייתא is about מנחות, not ביכורים. רב אדא בר אהבה pushes back from the פסוק, and רב משרשיא and רב אשי each defend רבה's answer. The גמרא then ties the question to the argument between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש, and shows how each of them reads the word מֵאַרְצְךָ. Finally, two ברייתות disagree about reciting over fruit from a roof, a ruin, a flowerpot or a ship. According to ריש לקיש, the גמרא settles each case by splitting it into a version that counts as land and a version that does not.

steps.title: Not mountain dates, not valley fruit
steps.stepSummary: The closing words of a teaching about ביכורים: they are not brought from dates of the mountains, nor from fruit of the valleys.
steps.simpleTranslation: Nor from dates that grow in the mountains, nor from fruit that grows in the valleys.
steps.whatsHappening: We are reading the last words of a teaching about which fruits may be brought as ביכורים. It says not to bring dates from the mountains, nor fruit from the valleys.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Valley fruit is of lower quality, so it is not the right choice for ביכורים. This sets up the next question: what happens if someone brought the lower-quality fruit anyway?

keyTerms.meaning: First fruits brought to the בית המקדש
Dates that grow in the mountains (lower quality)
Fruit that grows in the valleys (lower quality)

phrases.english: From dates that are in the mountains,
phrases.notes: This is the end of a longer teaching; just before this line it says 'one does not bring ביכורים except from the seven species, and not…'

phrases.english: and not from fruits that are in the valleys.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִתְּמָרִים שֶׁבֶּהָרִים וְלֹא מִפֵּירוֹת שֶׁבָּעֲמָקִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a teaching that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From the start, ביכורים should be brought from good-quality fruit, not from mountain dates or valley fruit, which Rashi says are thin and not the best.

steps.title: If brought anyway, it is not holy
steps.stepSummary: עולא rules that if someone brought the inferior fruit as ביכורים, it does not become holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: if he brought it, he did not make it holy.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא tells us what happens after the fact, when someone already brought the wrong fruit. His answer is that it does not become holy as ביכורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The teaching in step 1 could have been only advice about the best way to do the מצוה. עולא says it is stricter than that: this lower-quality fruit does not get the holiness of ביכורים at all, even after the fact.

keyTerms.meaning: If he already brought it (after the fact)
He did not make it holy; it does not get the holy status of ביכורים

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the ruling (שמעתא) that רבה teaches in the next step, and it is what רבי אחא בר אבא challenges.

phrases.english: Ulla said:
If he brought it, he did not make it holy.
phrases.notes: 'It' means the lower-quality fruit from the line before: mountain dates or valley fruit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא: אִם הֵבִיא לֹא קִידֵּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes further than step 1 by telling us what happens after the fact.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Inferior fruit brought as ביכורים does not become holy, even after the fact.

steps.title: An objection begins: the first of all meal offerings
steps.stepSummary: While רבה is teaching עולא's ruling, רבי אחא בר אבא objects by quoting a ברייתא. It says the שתי הלחם is the 'first offering', meaning it comes before every other מנחה from the new crop.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה sat and taught this ruling. רבי אחא בר אבא raised an objection to רבה from a ברייתא: 'A first offering' teaches that it should be the first of all the meal offerings. And so the פסוק says: 'When you bring a new meal offering to ה׳ on your שבועות.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבה is teaching עולא's ruling, and רבי אחא בר אבא starts to challenge it with a ברייתא. Here the גמרא is only beginning to quote the source; the actual point of the challenge comes in step 10.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads the words 'first offering' as a rule: the שתי הלחם of שבועות must be the very first מנחה brought from the new crop. It supports this with the פסוק calling it a 'new' מנחה.

keyTerms.meaning: A ruling or teaching (here, עולא's ruling)
'A first offering', the Torah's name for the שתי הלחם
'A new meal offering', the first one brought from the new grain
'And so it says', bringing a second פסוק as support

steps.confusionAlert: Do not expect the problem with עולא's ruling to show up yet. The ברייתא is long, and the גמרא only explains how it clashes with עולא after quoting all of it.

phrases.english: Rabba sat and was saying
this ruling,
phrases.notes: He means עולא's ruling: inferior fruit that was brought does not become holy.

phrases.aramaic: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַבִּי אַחָא בַּר אַבָּא לְרַבָּה:
phrases.english: Rabbi Aḥa bar Abba raised an objection to Rabba:
"A first offering" –
phrases.notes: ויקרא 2:12. Here it describes the שתי הלחם.

phrases.english: that it should be first of all the meal offerings,
and so it says:
"When you bring a new meal offering to the Lord on your Shavuot."
phrases.notes: במדבר 28:26

steps.triggerLanguage: יָתֵיב רַבָּה וְקָא אָמַר לַהּ לְהָא שְׁמַעְתָּא, אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַבִּי אַחָא בַּר אַבָּא לְרַבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a challenge to עולא's ruling from step 2, which רבה was teaching.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's ruling, as taught by רבה, that inferior fruit brought as ביכורים does not become holy
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא about the order of the שתי הלחם and ביכורים is being quoted. How it clashes with עולא is explained only after the whole ברייתא is quoted.

steps.title: First of the barley meal offerings too
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns from the double word 'new' that the שתי הלחם must come before barley meal offerings, not only before wheat ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: I only know that it is the 'new' one among wheat offerings. How do I know it is also the 'new' one among barley offerings? The Torah says 'new' and again 'new'. If the second one is not needed for the 'new' of wheat, apply it to the 'new' of barley.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and asks whether the שתי הלחם must also come before barley offerings. It answers yes, because the word 'new' appears twice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שתי הלחם is made of wheat, so the first 'new' teaches only that it comes before other wheat offerings. The Torah says 'new' a second time, and that extra word is not needed for wheat. So it teaches that the שתי הלחם also comes before barley offerings.

keyTerms.meaning: 'I only know...', meaning the פסוק so far teaches only this much
'From where do we know?', asking for a source
'The פסוק teaches', introducing the source
If a word is not needed for its own topic, use it to teach a different topic

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לִי אֶלָּא חֲדָשָׁה שֶׁל חִטִּים,
phrases.english: I have only the new one of wheat,
the new one of barley, from where?
The verse states "new," "new."
phrases.notes: The word 'new' appears in במדבר 28:26 and again in ויקרא 23:16.

phrases.aramaic: אִם אֵינוֹ עִנְיָן לַחֲדָשָׁה שֶׁל חִיטִּין –
phrases.english: If it is not needed for the matter of the new one of wheat –
apply it to the matter of the new one of barley.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין לִי אֶלָּא חֲדָשָׁה שֶׁל חִטִּים, חֲדָשָׁה שֶׁל שְׂעוֹרִים מִנַּיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא and extends 'first of all meal offerings' to barley offerings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שתי הלחם must come before both wheat and barley meal offerings from the new crop.

steps.title: Before the wheat first fruits
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא proves from a פסוק that the שתי הלחם must come before ביכורים of the wheat harvest.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that it comes before ביכורים? The פסוק says: 'And you shall make for yourself a festival of שבועות, the first fruits of the wheat harvest.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves to a new question: must the שתי הלחם also come before ביכורים? It brings a פסוק to show that it must, at least for wheat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק first mentions the festival of שבועות, whose special offering is the שתי הלחם, and only afterward the first fruits of the wheat harvest. That order teaches that the שתי הלחם comes before wheat ביכורים.

keyTerms.meaning: Comes first; goes before
The festival of שבועות, when the שתי הלחם is brought
The wheat harvest

phrases.english: And from where that it should precede the first fruits?
phrases.notes: 'It' is still the שתי הלחם.

phrases.english: The verse states:
"And you shall make for yourself a festival of Shavuot,
phrases.notes: שמות 34:22

phrases.english: the first fruits of the wheat harvest,"

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִנַּיִן שֶׁתְּהֵא קוֹדֶמֶת לְבִיכּוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from 'first of the meal offerings' to 'first before ביכורים'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שתי הלחם comes before ביכורים of the wheat harvest.

steps.title: Before the barley first fruits too
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא proves from a second פסוק that the שתי הלחם also comes before ביכורים of the barley harvest.
steps.simpleTranslation: I only know about the first fruits of the wheat harvest. How do I know about the barley harvest? The פסוק says: 'And the festival of the harvest, the first fruits of your work, which you sow in the field.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks whether barley ביכורים must also wait for the שתי הלחם. It brings a wider פסוק that covers everything sown in the field. The ברייתא keeps going in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק spoke only about wheat. This second פסוק speaks about everything 'you sow in the field', which includes barley. So the שתי הלחם must come before all ביכורים. The clash with עולא's ruling is explained in step 10.

keyTerms.meaning: The barley harvest
'The festival of the harvest', another name for שבועות
'The first fruits of your work', covering all crops you planted

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא teaches two things: the שתי הלחם is the first מנחה from the new crop, of wheat and of barley, and it comes before all ביכורים, of wheat and of barley. רבי אחא בר אבא brings this ברייתא to challenge עולא's ruling.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין לִי אֶלָּא בִּכּוּרֵי קְצִיר חִטִּים,
phrases.english: And I have only the first fruits of the wheat harvest,
the barley harvest, from where?
The verse states:
"And the festival of the harvest, the first fruits of your labors,
phrases.notes: שמות 23:16

phrases.english: which you will sow in the field."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין לִי אֶלָּא בִּכּוּרֵי קְצִיר חִטִּים, קְצִיר שְׂעוֹרִים מִנַּיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends step 5 from wheat ביכורים to barley ביכורים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שתי הלחם comes before all ביכורים of crops sown in the field, including barley.

steps.title: The שתי הלחם also comes before crops that grew by themselves
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds that the שתי הלחם comes first even before crops that sprouted on their own, learned from the word 'in the field'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says 'that you sow,' so I would only know about crops you planted. How do I know the rule also covers crops that came up by themselves? The verse adds 'in the field.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא keeps going. It widens the rule so it also covers crops nobody planted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק from step 6 says 'that you sow,' which could limit the rule to planted crops. The extra word 'in the field' teaches that crops that grew on their own are also included. So the שתי הלחם comes before their ביכורים too.

keyTerms.meaning: I would only know (from this verse) the following case
They came up by themselves, without being planted
The verse teaches (by adding a word)

phrases.english: I would only know about what you sow;
phrases.notes: This is the phrase 'אשר תזרע' (שמות 23:16) from the פסוק quoted in step 6.

phrases.english: crops that came up by themselves, from where do we know?
The verse says: "in the field."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין לִי אֶלָּא שֶׁתִּזְרַע, עָלוּ מֵאֲלֵיהֶן מִנַּיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא's list of things the שתי הלחם must come before.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שתי הלחם comes before ביכורים even of crops that grew by themselves.

steps.title: Including crops grown on a roof, in a ruin, in a flowerpot or on a ship
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא widens the rule beyond a field, to crops grown in unusual places, learned from 'the first fruits of all that is in their land'.
steps.simpleTranslation: So far I only know about crops grown in a field. How do I know to include crops grown on a roof, in a ruin, in a flowerpot or on a ship? The verse says 'the first fruits of all that is in their land.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds crops from strange, poor growing places to the list. This is the line רבי אחא בר אבא will use for his challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'In the field' could limit the rule to normal fields. The words 'all that is in their land' include crops grown anywhere, even on a roof or a ship. This matters because עולא said poor-quality fruit cannot become ביכורים.

keyTerms.meaning: To include (an extra case)
Roof
A ruined building
Flowerpot
Ship

steps.whyThisMatters: This list is the exact text רבי אחא בר אבא points to in the next step to challenge עולא.

phrases.english: I would only know about what grows in the field;
from where do we include what grows on a roof,
and in a ruin, and in a flowerpot, and on a ship?
The verse says: "The first fruits of all that is in their land."
phrases.notes: במדבר 18:13

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין לִי אֶלָּא בַּשָּׂדֶה, מִנַּיִן לְרַבּוֹת שֶׁבְּגַג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens the rule from step 7 beyond a field.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שתי הלחם comes first even before produce grown on a roof, in a ruin, in a flowerpot or on a ship.

steps.title: The שתי הלחם also comes before נסכים and tree fruit
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends by teaching that the שתי הלחם comes before נסכים and tree fruit, comparing the word 'your labors' in two parts of the same פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know the שתי הלחם comes before נסכים and tree fruit? Here it says 'the first fruits of your labors,' and later it says 'when you gather in your labors from the field.' Just as there it means נסכים and tree fruit, here too it means נסכים and tree fruit.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last part of the ברייתא. It adds wine for the נסכים and fruit from trees to the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same פסוק uses the word 'your labors' twice. At the end of the פסוק, 'gathering your labors from the field' means the harvest of grapes and tree fruit. So 'your labors' at the start of the פסוק means those too, and the שתי הלחם must come before them.

keyTerms.meaning: Wine poured on the מזבח with קרבנות
Fruit that grows on trees
Just as there, so too here (comparing two verses)

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא says the שתי הלחם comes before everything new: barley and wheat מנחות, ביכורים from anywhere, wine and tree fruit.

phrases.english: From where do we know that it should come before
libations and the fruit of the tree?
phrases.notes: The libations here are wine made from the new grape crop.

phrases.english: It says here: "The first fruits of your labors,"
phrases.notes: שמות 23:16

phrases.english: and it says there,
"When you gather in your labors from the field."
Just as there it means libations and tree fruit,
so too here it means libations and tree fruit.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִנַּיִן שֶׁתְּהֵא קוֹדֶמֶת לִנְסָכִים וּפֵירוֹת הָאִילָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא's list of things the שתי הלחם must come before.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שתי הלחם comes before new-crop נסכים and tree fruit.

steps.title: The ברייתא includes poor growing places, against עולא
steps.stepSummary: רבי אחא בר אבא points to the ברייתא's list of roof, ruin, flowerpot and ship, which seems to make low-quality produce fit for ביכורים, against עולא.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, the ברייתא teaches: what grows on a roof, in a ruin, in a flowerpot, and on a ship.
steps.whatsHappening: Now רבי אחא בר אבא explains why he quoted this whole ברייתא. He points to the one line that seems to contradict עולא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Crops from a roof, a ruin, a flowerpot or a ship are poor quality. If the ברייתא says the שתי הלחם must come before their ביכורים, then they must be fit to be ביכורים. That goes against עולא, who said inferior fruit brought as ביכורים does not become holy.

keyTerms.meaning: In any case, it teaches (pointing to the key line in a source)

steps.confusionAlert: The whole long ברייתא was quoted, but only this one line about the roof, ruin, flowerpot and ship is the actual challenge to עולא.

phrases.english: In any case, it teaches:
what grows on a roof, what grows in a ruin,
what grows in a flowerpot, and what grows on a ship.
phrases.notes: He leaves the point unsaid: these poor crops seem fit for ביכורים, unlike what עולא said.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָתָנֵי מִיהָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the line from step 8 to finish the challenge that began in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's ruling that inferior fruit brought as ביכורים does not become holy (step 2).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says the שתי הלחם comes before produce from poor growing places, which implies that such produce can be ביכורים.

steps.title: The later part of the ברייתא is about meal offerings
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that the later part of the ברייתא, with the roof, ruin, flowerpot and ship, is talking about מנחות, not ביכורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the later part of the ברייתא, we came to meal offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה defends עולא. He says the list of poor growing places is about מנחות, not ביכורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier part of the ברייתא spoke about ביכורים. The later part, which lists the roof, ruin, flowerpot and ship, is about grain for מנחות. Produce from those places can be used for מנחות but not as ביכורים, so עולא's ruling stands.

keyTerms.meaning: The later part of a source
We have come to (a new topic)
Meal offerings made from grain

steps.whatToRemember: עולא's ruling stands: the poor growing places in the ברייתא are about מנחות, not ביכורים.

phrases.english: In the later part, we have come to meal offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: סֵיפָא אֲתָאן לִמְנָחוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the source: the earlier and later parts of the ברייתא deal with different topics.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The roof, ruin, flowerpot and ship line means these crops are fit for ביכורים.
steps.terutzMaskana: That line is about מנחות. Such produce is fit for מנחות but not for ביכורים, so עולא is not contradicted.

steps.title: How can מנחות be eaten by the whole household?
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה challenges רבה. The פסוק says the whole pure household may eat it, but מנחות are eaten only by male כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה objected: If so, how does the פסוק fit when it says 'every pure one in your house may eat it'? If it means מנחות, those are eaten only by the males of the כהונה!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה attacks רבה's answer. רבה said this part of the ברייתא is about מנחות, but the פסוק it comes from does not seem to fit מנחות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'in your house' include a כהן's wife and daughters. מנחות may only be eaten by male כהנים, so a פסוק that lets the whole household eat cannot be talking about מנחות. That seems to bring us back to ביכורים, and then the question against עולא returns.

keyTerms.meaning: He objected to it, raising a strong challenge
If so, meaning if your answer is right
Every pure one in your house, which includes women of the כהן's family
The male כהנים

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה:
phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava objected to it:
phrases.notes: He is objecting to רבה's answer from the previous step, that this part is about מנחות.

phrases.english: If so, is this what is written:
"Every pure one in your house may eat it"?
phrases.notes: במדבר 18:13

phrases.english: But if it is about meal offerings,
they are eaten only by the males of the priesthood!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה: אִי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבה's answer from Step 11
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's claim that the end of the ברייתא and its פסוק are about מנחות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same פסוק lets the whole household eat, but מנחות are limited to male כהנים, so the פסוק cannot be about מנחות.

steps.title: The פסוק contains two separate teachings
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא says the פסוק works like two פסוקים. 'It shall be yours' is about מנחות, and 'every pure one in your house' is about ביכורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב משרשיא said: Two פסוקים are written here. It says 'it shall be yours,' and it says 'every pure one in your house may eat it.' How can both be true? This one is about ביכורים, and that one is about מנחות.
steps.whatsHappening: רב משרשיא defends רבה by splitting the פסוק into two parts, each teaching about something different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Inside the same פסוק there seems to be a contradiction: 'yours' means only the כהן himself, while 'your house' includes his family. So the household part must be about ביכורים, which the family may eat, and the 'yours' part, from which the ברייתא learns, is about מנחות, which only male כהנים eat. This way רבה's reading stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Two פסוקים are written, meaning the פסוק works like two separate teachings
It shall be yours, meaning for the כהן himself
How can this be? This sets up a way to fit both together
Here... here. Each part is talking about a different case

phrases.english: Rav Mesharshiyya said:
Two verses are written:
"It shall be yours,"
phrases.notes: This is from the same פסוק, במדבר 18:13. 'Yours' points to the כהן alone.

phrases.english: and it is written: "Every pure one in your house may eat it."
How can this be?
Here, it is about first fruits,
phrases.notes: This means the 'your house' part, since family members may eat ביכורים.

phrases.english: here, it is about meal offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב מְשַׁרְשְׁיָא: תְּרֵי קְרָאֵי כְּתִיבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 12
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the פסוק into two parts that teach different things
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The whole פסוק is one topic, so the household clause rules out מנחות.
steps.terutzMaskana: The 'yours' part is about מנחות, and the household part is about ביכורים.

steps.title: The whole פסוק is about offerings, and the end is about breads of a תודה
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers differently. The entire פסוק is about offerings, and the household part refers to the breads of a תודה, which the family may eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: The whole פסוק is about מנחות, and the end of the פסוק teaches about the breads of a תודה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives another way to defend רבה, without splitting the פסוק between ביכורים and מנחות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He keeps the whole פסוק on the topic of offerings. The breads of a תודה are a type of offering that is not limited to male כהנים, so 'every pure one in your house' fits them. That removes רב אדא בר אהבה's challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: All of it, the entire פסוק
The end part of the פסוק
The breads brought with a thanksgiving offering, which the כהן's family may eat

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
All of it is about meal offerings,
and with the end of the verse we come to the loaves of a thanks offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: כּוּלֵּיהּ בִּמְנָחוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to Step 12, different from רב משרשיא's
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the end of the פסוק to a specific kind of offering
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the פסוק is about offerings, the household clause cannot fit, because offerings belong only to male כהנים.
steps.terutzMaskana: The end of the פסוק is about the breads of a תודה, which the household may eat.
steps.whatToRemember: רבה's reading, that the ship and flowerpot part is about offerings, survives. רב משרשיא splits the פסוק between ביכורים and מנחות, while רב אשי keeps it all about offerings and explains the household part as the breads of a תודה.

steps.title: The same argument as רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the argument between עולא and רבי אחא בר אבא matches an earlier argument. רבי יוחנן says low-quality produce that was brought is not holy. ריש לקיש says it is holy, like a thin animal that was made holy as a sacrifice.
steps.simpleTranslation: This matches an argument: רבי יוחנן says that if he brought it, he did not make it holy. ריש לקיש says that if he brought it, he did make it holy, and it is treated like a thin animal among sacrifices.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא connects the argument between עולא and רבי אחא בר אבא, about low-quality produce as ביכורים, to an argument between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree that one should not bring low-quality produce as ביכורים to begin with. The question is what happens if someone already did. רבי יוחנן says it does not become holy at all. ריש לקיש says it does, just as a thin, weak animal should not be given as a sacrifice, but becomes holy if someone does give it.

keyTerms.meaning: This matches an argument, an earlier dispute on the same issue
He made it holy
A thin, weak animal
Holy offerings and sacrifices

steps.confusionAlert: ריש לקיש does not say it is fine to bring low-quality produce to begin with. He only says that after the fact it becomes holy, like a thin animal.
steps.whatToRemember: The argument over low-quality produce as ביכורים comes down to an after-the-fact question: רבי יוחנן says it does not become holy, and ריש לקיש says it does, just like a thin animal given as a sacrifice.

phrases.english: It is the same as a dispute:
phrases.notes: It means the argument between עולא and רבי אחא בר אבא matches this one.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר – אִם הֵבִיא לֹא קִדֵּשׁ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan says: If he brought it, he did not consecrate it;
phrases.notes: 'It' means the low-quality produce, like dates from the mountains or produce from the valleys, brought as ביכורים.

phrases.aramaic: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר – אִם הֵבִיא קִדֵּשׁ,
phrases.english: Reish Lakish says: If he brought it, he consecrated it;
it is like a gaunt animal among sacrificial offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּפְלוּגְתָּא: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending עולא, the גמרא places the whole argument inside a known dispute
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Low-quality produce brought as ביכורים: according to רבי יוחנן it is not holy, and according to ריש לקיש it is holy, like a thin animal given as a sacrifice.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the argument is not only about a ברייתא. It is about a wider question: does something that should not have been given still become holy if someone gives it anyway?

steps.title: What is רבי יוחנן's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says ריש לקיש's view makes sense because he gave a reason. Then it asks what reason רבי יוחנן has.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש's view is understandable, since he gave his reason. But what is רבי יוחנן's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. It asks for the source behind רבי יוחנן's view that low-quality ביכורים are not holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש already explained himself: it is like a thin animal that was made holy. רבי יוחנן gave no reason, so the גמרא wants to know where his view comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, this one is understandable (opens a contrast with a difficulty)
What is the reason?

phrases.english: Granted, Reish Lakish, as he stated the reason.
phrases.notes: His reason was the comparison to a thin animal that was made holy (step 15).

phrases.english: But Rabbi Yochanan, what is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ כִּדְאָמַר טַעְמָא אֶלָּא רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind one side of the argument quoted in step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source or reason for רבי יוחנן's view that low-quality ביכורים are not holy.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר explains רבי יוחנן from the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says that 'from the first' means not every first fruit, and 'from your land' means not every part of your land.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: I saw רבי יוחנן in a dream, so I am saying a good thing. The פסוק says 'from the first', which means not all first fruits. It says 'from your land', which means not all of your land.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers the question by finding רבי יוחנן's source in the פסוק about ביכורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The little letter מ (meaning 'from', or 'some of') shows the Torah means only part of the fruits and only part of the land. So fruit that does not fit, like low-quality produce, is simply not ביכורים, and it does not become holy.

keyTerms.meaning: A fine, proper statement
The first fruits
From your land, meaning from some of your land

steps.confusionAlert: The dream is not the proof. It only shows that רבי אלעזר felt sure about his explanation. The proof is the extra מ in the פסוק.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
I saw Rabbi Yochanan in a dream,
so I am saying a proper matter.
phrases.notes: He means that seeing his teacher in a dream gives him confidence that this explanation is right.

phrases.english: The verse says: 'From the first,' but not all the first.
phrases.notes: דברים 26:2

phrases.english: 'From your land,' but not all of your land.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא מֵרֵאשִׁית וְלֹא כׇּל רֵאשִׁית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra מ in מֵרֵאשִׁית and מֵאַרְצְךָ limits ביכורים to some fruits and some places, so unfit produce never becomes holy.

steps.title: What does ריש לקיש learn from 'your land'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how ריש לקיש uses the word 'your land', since he does not use it the way רבי יוחנן does.
steps.simpleTranslation: And ריש לקיש, what does he do with this word 'your land'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. It asks how ריש לקיש explains the word that רבי יוחנן used as his source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every word in the Torah is expected to teach something. If ריש לקיש does not learn רבי יוחנן's limit from 'your land', he must use it for something else.

keyTerms.meaning: What does he do with it? (How does he use this word?)

phrases.aramaic: וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ, הַאי ״אַרְצְךָ״ מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ?
phrases.english: And Reish Lakish, this 'your land', what does he do with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ הַאי אַרְצְךָ מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to the other side and asks how it uses the source from step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What ריש לקיש learns from the word אַרְצְךָ.

steps.title: ריש לקיש uses 'land' to limit ביכורים to the seven species
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש needs the word for the ברייתא of רבן גמליאל בר רבי, who links 'land' here to 'land' in the praise of ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs it for what was taught: רבן גמליאל the son of רבי says, 'land' is said here and 'land' is said there. Just as there it means the praise of the land, so too here it means the praise of the land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that ריש לקיש uses 'your land' for a גזירה שוה. It teaches that ביכורים come only from the fruits the Torah praises ארץ ישראל for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'land' appears in the ביכורים פסוק and also in the פסוק praising the land with the שבעת המינים. Linking the two teaches that ביכורים are brought only from those seven species. So for ריש לקיש, the word is already used up for this.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it (for a different teaching)
A link between two פסוקים that use the same word
The praise of the land, meaning the שִׁבְעַת הַמִּינִים

phrases.english: He needs it for what was taught in a ברייתא:
Rabban Gamliel, son of Rabbi, says:
'Land' is said here, and 'land' is said there.
phrases.notes: 'Here' is the ביכורים פסוק. 'There' is the praise of the land with the seven species (דברים 8:8).

phrases.english: Just as there it means the praise of the land,
so too here it means the praise of the land.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְכִדְתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ריש לקיש uses אַרְצְךָ for a גזירה שוה that limits ביכורים to the שבעת המינים.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן learns from both 'land' and 'from land'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן also learns the seven-species rule. He takes it from the word 'land', and his own limit from the extra 'from'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one learns from 'land' and from 'from land'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains, very briefly, how רבי יוחנן also has the seven-species rule. He splits the word into two parts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah could have written just 'your land' but wrote 'from your land'. רבי יוחנן uses 'land' for the גזירה שוה and the extra 'from' to teach 'not all your land'. So one word gives him two teachings.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one (the other side of the argument)

steps.confusionAlert: This line is very short. It hides both a question (where does רבי יוחנן learn the seven species?) and its answer (from splitting 'land' and 'from land').

phrases.english: And the other one learns 'land' and 'from land'.
phrases.notes: 'The other one' is רבי יוחנן: 'land' gives the seven species, and the extra 'from' gives 'not all your land'.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ אֶרֶץ מֵאֶרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns back to רבי יוחנן and shows he can also keep the גזירה שוה from step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting one word into two teachings
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since רבי יוחנן used מֵאַרְצְךָ for 'not all your land', he would have no source for the seven-species rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: He uses 'land' for the גזירה שוה and the extra 'from' for his own limit.

steps.title: ריש לקיש does not split 'land' from 'from land'
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש does not learn anything from the difference between 'land' and 'from land', so the word gives him only the גזירה שוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one does not learn anything from 'land' versus 'from land'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why ריש לקיש does not get רבי יוחנן's extra teaching. He does not treat the 'from' as a separate lesson.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For ריש לקיש, מֵאַרְצְךָ is one word, and all of it is used for the גזירה שוה. So he has no source to say low-quality produce is excluded, and that fits his view that such produce does become holy.

keyTerms.meaning: He does not learn it from there (it does not mean that to him)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן reads מֵאַרְצְךָ as two lessons: 'land' gives the seven species, and 'from' gives 'not all your land', so poor produce is not holy. ריש לקיש reads it as one lesson, the seven species only.
steps.whyThisMatters: The whole argument about whether low-quality ביכורים become holy comes down to whether the small letter מ teaches something of its own.

phrases.english: And the other one does not learn anything from 'land' versus 'from land'.
phrases.notes: 'The other one' here is ריש לקיש.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ אֶרֶץ מֵאֶרֶץ לָא מַשְׁמַע לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives ריש לקיש's side in response to רבי יוחנן's split reading in step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ריש לקיש does not draw a separate lesson from the extra מ, so for him the word teaches only the גזירה שוה.

steps.title: Two teachings disagree about reciting over unusual fruit
steps.stepSummary: One ברייתא says fruit from a roof, a ruin, a flowerpot, or a ship is brought and the declaration is recited. Another ברייתא says it is brought but not recited.
steps.simpleTranslation: One ברייתא teaches: fruit that grew on a roof, in a ruin, in a flowerpot, or on a ship is brought, and the owner recites. Another ברייתא teaches: he brings it but does not recite.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new section by quoting two ברייתות that seem to contradict each other. This sets up the next steps, where the גמרא will try to settle the contradiction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both ברייתות agree that this fruit is brought to the מקדש. They disagree only about whether the owner says the בכורים declaration. Since the same four cases appear in both, there is a direct clash.

keyTerms.meaning: He brings the fruit and recites the declaration
He brings the fruit but does not recite
A ship
First fruits brought to the מקדש

phrases.english: One baraita teaches:
Produce that grew on a roof, or in a ruin,
or in a flowerpot, or on a ship –
he brings it and recites.
phrases.notes: "Recites" means saying the thank-you passage over בכורים, דברים 26:5–10.

phrases.english: And another baraita teaches:
he brings it but does not recite.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי חֲדָא וְתַנְיָא אִידַּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section about fruit from unusual places, which ties into the debate about inferior produce.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two ברייתות disagree about whether one recites over fruit from a roof, a ruin, a flowerpot, or a ship. Both agree that it is brought.

steps.title: Roof of a cave versus roof of a house
steps.stepSummary: According to ריש לקיש, the roof clash is settled: the ברייתא that says he recites means a cave's roof, and the one that says he does not means a house's roof.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, according to ריש לקיש, the roof against the roof is no problem: this ברייתא is talking about the roof of a cave, and that one is talking about the roof of a house.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts settling the clash according to ריש לקיש, beginning with the roof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A cave's roof is really part of the ground, so fruit grown there counts as from the land, and he recites. A house's roof is a building, so he brings but does not recite. The word בשלמא hints that this works smoothly for ריש לקיש, which may not be true for the other view.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, it works well (for this view)
It is not difficult
The roof of a cave, which is really ground
The roof of a house, which is a building

steps.confusionAlert: Both ברייתות say "he brings." For ריש לקיש the only question is reciting, not whether the fruit counts as בכורים at all.

phrases.english: Granted, according to Reish Lakish,
roof against roof is not difficult:
this one is about the roof of a cave,
phrases.notes: The top of a cave is solid earth, so it counts as real ground.

phrases.english: that one is about the roof of a house.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ, גַּג אַגַּג לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins resolving the contradiction raised in step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each ברייתא is about a different kind of roof.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות seemed to speak about the same roof and to rule in opposite ways.
steps.terutzMaskana: A cave's roof counts as land, so he recites. A house's roof does not, so he brings without reciting.

steps.title: Worked ruin versus unworked ruin
steps.stepSummary: The ruin clash is settled: he recites over a ruin that is being worked, and does not recite over one that is left unworked.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ruin against the ruin is no problem: here it is a ruin that is worked, and there it is a ruin that is not worked.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues with the second case and settles the ruin the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ruin that is farmed acts like a normal field, so its fruit gets the full declaration. A ruin that is not farmed is not treated like a normal field, so he brings the fruit but does not recite.

keyTerms.meaning: A ruin, a destroyed area
Worked, farmed
Here... there (one ברייתא... the other)

phrases.english: Ruin against ruin is not difficult:
here it is about a ruin that is worked,
there it is about a ruin that is not worked.

steps.triggerLanguage: חוּרְבָּה אַחוּרְבָּה – לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same splitting method as step 23, now for the ruin.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: a worked ruin versus an unworked ruin.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות seemed to be about the same kind of ruin.
steps.terutzMaskana: He recites over a farmed ruin. Over an unfarmed one, he brings but does not recite.

steps.title: Pot with a hole versus pot without a hole
steps.stepSummary: The flowerpot clash is settled: he recites over a pot with a hole, and does not recite over a pot with no hole.
steps.simpleTranslation: The flowerpot against the flowerpot is no problem: here it is a pot with a hole, and there it is a pot without a hole.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the third case, the flowerpot, by splitting it into two kinds of pots.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A pot with a hole lets the plant draw from the ground below, so it counts as growing from the land, and he recites. A sealed pot cuts the plant off from the ground, so he brings but does not recite.

keyTerms.meaning: A flowerpot
Having a hole (perforated)
Without a hole (sealed)

steps.whatToRemember: For ריש לקיש, the roof, the ruin, and the flowerpot are all settled by splitting each into a case that counts as land (he recites) and a case that does not (he brings only). The next step settles the ship the same way.

phrases.english: Flowerpot against flowerpot is not difficult:
here it is about one with a hole,
phrases.notes: The hole lets the roots reach the ground underneath.

phrases.english: there it is about one without a hole.

steps.triggerLanguage: עָצִיץ אַעָצִיץ – לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The third case settled with the same splitting method as steps 23 and 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: a pot with a hole versus a pot without one.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות seemed to be about the same kind of flowerpot.
steps.terutzMaskana: A pot with a hole is connected to the ground, so he recites. A sealed pot is not, so he brings without reciting.

steps.title: Wooden ship versus clay ship
steps.stepSummary: The two ברייתות about fruit grown on a ship do not clash. The one that says he recites means a wooden ship. The one that says he does not recite means a clay ship.
steps.simpleTranslation: Ship against ship is not a problem. Here it is a ship made of wood, and there it is a ship made of clay.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the fourth and last clash between the two ברייתות, the one about a ship. It splits the case into a wooden ship and a clay ship.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the roof, the ruin and the flowerpot before it, the ship is not one single case. The ברייתא that says the declaration of ביכורים is recited is talking about a wooden ship. The ברייתא that says it is not recited is talking about a clay ship. This follows the same pattern as the pot with a hole and the pot with no hole in the step before.

keyTerms.meaning: A ship or boat
It is not a problem. The two sources can both be right.
Wood
Earthenware, meaning baked clay

steps.whatToRemember: According to ריש לקיש, all four clashes (roof, ruin, flowerpot, ship) are settled the same way. Each case has one version that counts as connected to the land, so he recites, and one version that does not, so he brings the fruit but does not recite.

phrases.english: Ship against ship is not difficult:
here, it is a ship made of wood,
there, it is a ship made of earthenware.

steps.triggerLanguage: סְפִינָה אַסְּפִינָה – לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same pattern as steps 23 to 25, now applied to the fourth item, the ship.
